Installation & Usage
====================

.. contents:: On this page
   :depth: 2
   :local:

Prerequisites
-------------

.. list-table::
    :header-rows: 1
    :widths: 20 20 60

    * - Dependency
       - Minimum version
       - Notes
    * - CMake
       - 3.18
       - 4.x recommended
    * - C++ compiler
       - C++23-capable
       - AppleClang >= 17, GCC >= 13, Clang >= 17
    * - LibTorch
       - 2.0
       - Standalone **or** PyTorch headers
    * - Ninja *(optional)*
       - any
       - Faster than ``make``

.. note::

   The program is developed and tested against the **standalone LibTorch 2.11.0**
   installed at ``/usr/local``.  If you have a PyTorch Python installation, CMake
   auto-detection will find it as a fallback, but the standalone build is preferred
   because it avoids duplicate-header conflicts.

Building
--------

1. **Clone / enter the source tree**

   .. code-block:: bash

      git clone <repo-url> hftest
      cd hftest

2. **Configure with CMake**

   .. code-block:: bash

      cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

   CMake will search for a LibTorch installation in this order:

   a. ``/usr/local/share/cmake/Torch`` (standalone)
   b. ``$(python3 -c "...sitepackages")/torch/share/cmake/Torch``
   c. The path given by ``-DTORCH_HINT=<cmake-dir>`` on the command line.

   A successful configuration prints:

   .. code-block:: none

      -- Using Torch cmake dir: /usr/local/share/cmake/Torch
      -- Found Torch: ...

3. **Compile**

   .. code-block:: bash

      cmake --build build -j$(nproc)

   The binary is placed at ``build/hftest``.

4. **Run the bundled test**

   .. code-block:: bash

      cd build && ./hftest ../input.toml

   Expected output (abridged):

   .. code-block:: none

      Converged: YES   Iterations: 12
      Total energy: -75.0171735279 Ha

Input File Format
-----------------

The program reads a `TOML <https://toml.io>`_ file.  The minimal structure is:

.. code-block:: toml

   # ── Molecular system ──────────────────────────────────────────────
   [system]
   charge       = 0     # net charge (integer, default 0)
   multiplicity = 1     # 2S+1 (1 = singlet → RHF; >1 → UHF)
   basis        = "sto-3g"

   # ── Geometry (Cartesian Angstroms) ────────────────────────────────
   [[atoms]]
   symbol = "O"
   x = 0.000000
   y = 0.000000
   z = 0.117790

   [[atoms]]
   symbol = "H"
   x = 0.000000
   y = 0.757200
   z = -0.471160

   [[atoms]]
   symbol = "H"
   x =  0.000000
   y = -0.757200
   z = -0.471160

   # ── SCF settings (all optional) ───────────────────────────────────
   [scf]
   max_iter    = 100      # maximum number of SCF iterations
   convergence = 1e-9     # energy + density convergence threshold
   diis_size   = 8        # DIIS subspace size
   screen_tol  = 1e-10    # Schwarz screening threshold for ERIs

.. list-table:: TOML keys reference
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 15 15 45

   * - Key
     - Section
     - Default
     - Description
   * - ``charge``
     - ``[system]``
     - ``0``
     - Net molecular charge.
   * - ``multiplicity``
     - ``[system]``
     - ``1``
     - Spin multiplicity (2S+1). ``1`` → RHF; ``≥ 2`` → UHF.
   * - ``basis``
     - ``[system]``
     - *(required)*
     - Basis set name, matched case-insensitively to files in
       ``basis/`` directory.
   * - ``max_iter``
     - ``[scf]``
     - ``100``
     - Maximum number of SCF iterations before declaring failure.
   * - ``convergence``
     - ``[scf]``
     - ``1e-8``
       - Convergence criterion applied simultaneously to
          :math:`|\Delta E|` and :math:`\mathrm{RMS}(\Delta\mathbf{P})`.
   * - ``diis_size``
     - ``[scf]``
     - ``8``
     - Number of Fock/error vector pairs retained in DIIS memory.
   * - ``screen_tol``
     - ``[scf]``
     - ``1e-10``
     - Schwarz inequality screening tolerance for two-electron
       integral shell quartets.

Basis Set Files
---------------

Basis sets live in the ``basis/`` directory.  Files use the
*Basis Set Exchange* (BSE) **Gaussian-format** layout, identical to what
BSE exports when you select "Gaussian94" format.  The filename must
match the ``basis`` key in the TOML file (case-insensitive):

.. code-block:: none

   basis/
   ├── sto-3g
   ├── 6-31g(d)
   ├── cc-pvdz
   └── def2-tzvpp
   ...

Bundled basis sets span H through Xe and include Pople, Dunning
correlation-consistent, def2, and LANL families.

.. note::

   LANL effective-core-potential (ECP) blocks inside basis files are
   **silently skipped** — only the valence Gaussian contractions are
   loaded.  ECP integrals are not yet implemented.

Selecting RHF vs UHF
---------------------

The choice is made automatically from ``multiplicity``:

* ``multiplicity = 1`` and an **even** number of electrons → **RHF**
* ``multiplicity ≥ 2`` **or** an **odd** number of electrons → **UHF**

UHF output additionally reports :math:`\langle \hat{S}^2 \rangle` and
flags spin contamination when

.. math::

   \langle \hat{S}^2 \rangle_\text{UHF} - \langle \hat{S}^2 \rangle_\text{exact}
   > 0.1 \cdot \langle \hat{S}^2 \rangle_\text{exact}\,.

Example: open-shell H atom
--------------------------

.. code-block:: toml

   [system]
   charge       = 0
   multiplicity = 2
   basis        = "sto-3g"

   [[atoms]]
   symbol = "H"
   x = 0.0
   y = 0.0
   z = 0.0

Expected output:

.. code-block:: none

   Converged: YES   Iterations: 2
   Total energy:   -0.4665818504 Ha
   <S²> exact:  0.7500
   <S²> UHF:    0.7500
